root_idea.summary: A root of separation and drawing away: something recoils, withdraws, or moves off from its place.
root_idea.development: The physical idea of moving away extends to fright, aversion, and withdrawal; movement away also yields departure and the collective terms for people who go forth, mobilize, or support an undertaking. Swelling is explained as flesh or skin drawing away from an affected part.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested participial form with active and passive readings.
Distinct Quran-attested collective noun for a mobilized company or force.
Distinct Quran-attested verbal noun denoting aversion.

senses.definition: To go forth, depart, or advance, especially to go to war or undertake an affair.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic Form I occurrences, the subject is commanded or described as going forth, commonly in the context of collective mobilization; the imperative, imperfect, and perfect forms are grammatical variants of this use.

quranic_forms.public_pos_label: Active participle / adjective · with a passive Quranic reading

senses.usage_conditions: The active reading of the Quranic participle presents the subjects as themselves fleeing in alarm.

senses.definition: Made to take fright; scared away.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported passive reading of the same Quranic form understands it as describing something frightened or driven into flight.

senses.definition: A group or party, especially a small group able to go forth.
senses.usage_conditions: A collective or quasi-plural noun. Classical descriptions often specify a small number of men, while the Quranic occurrences also use it for a group of jinn; the exact numerical range is not uniform in the lexical evidence.

senses.definition: A company or force going forth for an undertaking, especially war; a mobilized host.
senses.usage_conditions: A collective noun for people assembled or hastening to act. In its Quranic occurrence, the surrounding expression presents the force as numerous.

senses.definition: Aversion, recoil, or turning away from something.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun denoting a response of shrinking or withdrawing, including aversion from a message, truth, or other object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an animal or other beast: to take fright, flee, or run away erratically; to become refractory and go off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of wild animals, camels, and beasts of carriage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recede, withdraw, or become remote or aloof from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive or intransitive construction describing separation from a thing or place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become swollen, as skin, flesh, an eye, or a wound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The swelling is explained as the flesh or skin drawing away from the affected part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flee or betake oneself to God through fear, seeking protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed construction with إِلَى and a motive of fear or refuge-seeking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become separated or dispersed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes members of a group or animals becoming divided and going apart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The day of departure from Minā by the pilgrims.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pilgrimage expression; the first and last days of departure may be distinguished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go forth to aid or succour someone; when called upon, to comply by going forth in support.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A support or relief construction related to going forth for another's assistance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone or an animal take fright and flee; to scare away or drive away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used literally of animals, including driving camels or livestock from pasture, and figuratively of conduct that drives people away through roughness or violence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give a child a disliked nickname or name of reproach as a means of warding off the evil eye or spirits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A protective naming custom, not ordinary naming terminology.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shun or avoid one another and regard one another with aversion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal construction is reported as possibly post-Classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be incongruous or discordant with one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative reciprocal use, also reported as possibly post-Classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels: to take fright, run away erratically, and become separated or dispersed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form IV usage recorded for camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incite, summon, or invite people to go forth, especially to war; to demand or seek their aid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May also express imposing the duty of going forth on people of differing circumstances or capacities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Aversion or shrinking from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from نَفَرٌ meaning a group or party.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man's near kinsmen or household group who go with him to war or support him in a crisis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to close relations acting collectively on behalf of one of their members.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An object hung upon a child to repel or ward off the evil eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A protective charm or amulet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imitative form denoting corroboration or strengthening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized echo-form associated with other expressions of corroboration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disposition or tendency of an animal to take fright and flee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a beast that is prone to sudden flight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A supporting company, auxiliaries, or people accompanying someone to fight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Focuses on the people who provide support or accompany a leader, rather than simply on departure itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Averse, shrinking from, or avoiding something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial adjective used of a person or disposition; the lexical evidence does not restrict the object to any particular gender or class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who drives people away or makes them averse through roughness or violence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle of Form II, used for conduct that provokes flight or aversion.

cautions: The Quranic form مُسْتَنْفِرٌ is tagged as an active participle in the supplied morphology, while the lexical evidence records both active and passive readings; both are therefore shown as senses of the Quranic form.
The supplied QAC occurrences include Form I نَفَرَ but no Form X occurrence; اِسْتَنْفَرَ is retained as a broader lexical meaning even though Lane relates it to the Quranic mobilization context.
The exact numerical range traditionally associated with نَفَرٌ varies in the lexical evidence, so the Quranic noun is defined generally as a group or party.
